answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it can trade. Think of the stake as an onyx seal: unique, hard to forge, and expensive to duplicate at scale. Every transaction leaves a public mirror of behavior, so peers can compare an agent's history against its claims. A real agent builds a steady pulse of consistent, useful work, while fake identities show thin, synchronized activity with no track record. Creating many credible histories costs far more than the rewards they could extract, so sybils become unprofitable.
